_comment: designs/500... design04_4source (2026-09-09): design03_realscale reservoir (600x27.5 Nd:YAG) but with 4 SEPARATE input strips across the 27.5 um aperture (y=+-10.31, +-3.44; width 4.0, pitch 6.875), Ey 1064 nm CW. sweep_sources co-drives all 4 at the same amplitude. For the SPACE reservoir: characterize the stationary spatial nonlinear map; operate near I_sat (sum of 4 channels ~ I_sat, i.e. per-channel ~I_sat/4). Amplitude levels set by the sweep --levels (TBD, near-I_sat regime). Pump source_pump unchanged (Ez 808 amp 50).

guide_1._comment: input stub, 27.5 um tall = design01's 5 um x sqrt(30). n step 1.82/1.77 gives NA 0.42 (acceptance 25 deg), same as design01 — the strips in design03b will overrun it and bounce, exactly as the 1 um strips did in design01d (footprint/half-width ratio 2.19 in both).

crystal._comment: Nd:YAG at LITERAL 1 at.% doping. SGMA 6.2e-7 x N3_0 30 over 600 um -> gL = 2.32, identical to design01's scaled-doping gL. Population grid resolution stays 10.

sted._comment: Starts fully inverted (N3_0=30, N1_0=0), same justification as design01: 230 us storage means a pre-pumped crystal simply IS full when a ps-scale signal arrives, and 230 us = 7e10 t.u. is unreachable in-sim, so the upper level effectively does not decay over the run. Consequence for reading the sweep: saturation here is a FINITE STORED INVERSION being burned, not a steady-state tau balance. The real I_sat = h*nu/(sigma_em*tau) = 2.9 kW/cm2 comes from real constants, NOT from this axis.

source_1._comment: input strip 1, y=-10.3125 um, width 4.0 um

source_pump._comment: 808 nm CW pump entering from above, y-normal sheet along the whole 600 um top edge. Ez, orthogonal to the Ey signal so they never interfere directly; the crystal is isotropic so the pump still drives 1->4. Amplitude 50 unchanged from design01 — the sheet is 30x longer but the per-unit-length pump intensity is the same, so the local refill rate matches.

monitor_1._comment: input reference line. Sensors kept deliberately minimal (two 1Ddft lines + one point): a 10000 t.u. run on a 606x32 um cell with line snapshots or population dumps would be many GB per task.

monitor_2._comment: output line. monitor_2/monitor_1 at 1.064 is the single-pass gain.

snap_point._comment: exit time trace — this is what the pilot is really for: the envelope flattening time sets dft_t_start for the production sweep. If it has not flattened by 6000, raise run_until before trusting any gain number.

source_2._comment: input strip 2, y=-3.4375 um, width 4.0 um

source_3._comment: input strip 3, y=3.4375 um, width 4.0 um

source_4._comment: input strip 4, y=10.3125 um, width 4.0 um
